results.title: Today’s front pages: Friday, November 6, 2026
results.content: Myjoyonline.com brings you the front pages of the various newspapers across the country.

results.title: GPCL MD defends record, challenges predecessor over GH¢22m VAT debt
results.content: The Managing Director of the Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) has defended his administration’s record, challenging his predecessor, David Asante Boateng, to account for about GH¢22 million in outstanding Value Added Tax (VAT) liabilities and the company's financial position at the time he left office. The exchange follows the current MD's appearance at the Government Accountability Series on November 2, 2026, where he outlined GPCL's achievements and challenges. Mr Boateng had reportedly claimed that he built the company from nothing into a profitable institution and advised his successor to “think more and talk less”.

results.title: IFS calls for reforms in 2027 budget to boost domestic revenue mobilisation
results.content: The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) is warning that Ghana’s weak domestic revenue mobilisation is undermining the country’s capacity to finance critical infrastructure, improve public sector wages and accelerate national development. results.title: Africa’s next great traveller is already at the departure gate
results.content: For decades, Africa’s tourism industry has been preoccupied with bringing the world to its shores. A landmark Skift study commissioned by Millat Group suggests that the continent’s next great tourism opportunity may lie in the opposite direction: the African traveller going out.

results.title: Four decades of biodiversity conservation: Goziir calls for greater support to sustain long-standing environmental efforts
results.content: For more than four decades, since 1980, the people of Goziir in the Nandom Municipality of the Upper West Region have demonstrated a remarkable commitment to environmental conservation by maintaining a strong community-wide culture of bushfire prevention and protecting local biodiversity.

results.title: Australia’s oldest department store David Jones folds after 188 years
results.content: David Jones, Australia's oldest department store chain, has gone into voluntary administration, putting thousands of jobs at risk.

results.title: James Barnor named recipient of Sony World Photography Awards 2027 honour
results.content: Ghanaian photographer James Barnor has been named recipient of the Outstanding Contribution to Photography award at the 2027 Sony World Photography Awards. The announcement marks the 20th edition of the awards, which celebrate photographers from around the world and recognise their contributions to the medium. results.title: Education Ministry, Gates Foundation consider partnership to boost Ghana’s malaria research
results.content: More than GH¢2 billion has been absorbed by the government to limit the impact of rising international petroleum prices on Ghanaian consumers, the Chief Executive Officer of the National Petroleum Authority (NPA), Godwin Kudzo Tameklo, has said.

results.title: Accra’s disturbing potholes endanger motorists
results.content: Some major roads and highways in Accra have developed serious potholes, making driving on those roads dangerous for motorists and other road users.

results.content: Ghanaian seafarers could gain access to additional employment opportunities in Canada following an agreement between the two countries to recognise each other’s professional maritime certificates. The arrangement was formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed at the headquarters of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) in London on November 5, 2026. results.title: Prof Beyuo takes responsibility for medical bills of 12 injured in Hamile unrest
results.content: Lambussie MP Professor Titus Beyuo has offered to pay the hospital bills of 12 people injured in the violence that erupted in Hamile following a deadly explosion in the Upper West Region.

results.title: Opoku-Agyemang calls for prosecution of perpetrators of sex-for-jobs abuse
results.content: Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has called for prompt investigations into sexual exploitation allegations in workplaces and educational institutions, stressing that anyone found guilty must be appropriately sanctioned.

results.title: Assafuah rejects Mahama’s invitation to World Cup visa probe committee
results.content: Member of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee Ranking Member, Vincent Ekow Assafuah, has rejected an invitation to appear before a committee set up by President John Dramani Mahama to investigate alleged irregularities in the 2026 FIFA World Cup visa acquisition process.

results.title: Mahama sets monthly review of road crash data to measure TraffiTech results
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama says the government will use monthly road accident figures to determine whether the newly introduced TraffiTech system is reducing crashes and preventing deaths on Ghana’s roads.

results.title: Car dealers block Kwashieman footbridge walkway, exposing pedestrians to danger
results.content: Roadside car dealers have blocked the pedestrian walkway leading to the Kwashieman footbridge in Accra, making it difficult for pedestrians to cross the N1 highway.

results.title: Ada drug haul: Navy intercepts two boats with 4.7 tonnes of suspected cannabis
results.content: A naval operation at the Ada Estuary has led to the seizure of 117 sacks of substances suspected to be Indian hemp, with an estimated weight of 4.7 tonnes and a street value exceeding US$1 million.

results.title: Chinese malls taking 60% of Ghana’s retail market – GUTA laments
results.content: The Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA) has raised concerns over the rapid expansion of Chinese-owned shopping malls in the country, claiming that they are taking an estimated 60 per cent share of the market and putting pressure on local businesses. results.title: World Cup raffle: Minority seeks audit over GH¢ contributions and match tickets
results.content: The Minority in Parliament is calling for an independent examination of the World Cup Bonanza Raffle, accusing the government of failing to account adequately for money collected from participants and demanding full disclosure of the promotion’s financial arrangements.

results.title: Adomako-Mensah says government ignored warnings over GH¢1 fuel levy
results.content: The government’s decision to introduce the GH¢1-per-litre fuel levy has contributed to the pressure now facing petroleum consumers, with the Minority in Parliament insisting that the difficulties could have been avoided if its earlier concerns had been considered.

results.title: EU says galamsey is eroding gains from development projects in Ghana
results.content: The European Union has raised concerns that illegal mining is reversing development gains in Ghana, warning that the practice is threatening investments in agriculture, sanitation, security and environmental protection.

results.title: Mahama briefs diaspora Ghanaians on $1 billion housing mortgage scheme
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has urged the Ghanaians in the Caribbean to take advantage of a $1 billion mortgage initiative designed to help citizens at home and abroad to become homeowners.

results.title: Finance Minister applauds Nyakrom Community Bank for pioneering banking initiative
results.content: Dr Cassel Ato Forson, the Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, has applauded the Nyakrom Community Bank PLC for its pioneering initiative in Rural /Community banking.

results.title: Japan Motors CEO Salem Kalmoni unveils his 6 rules for business success
results.content: Business mogul Salem Kalmoni says the lessons he has gathered from years of managing a family-owned enterprise have taught him that success depends as much on avoiding costly mistakes as it does on pursuing growth.

results.title: Moreshet Foundation joins Global Partnership for Education
results.content: Moreshet Foundation has joined the Private Foundations Constituency of the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), marking a significant step in its efforts to advance education and strengthen education systems globally. results.title: Cenpower celebrates its journey and contribution to Ghana’s energy sector
results.content: Cenpower Generation Ltd (Cenpower), owner of the 350 MW Kpone Independent Power Plant (KIPP), has marked a significant milestone in its development journey by celebrating the decade since the power plant's sod-cutting ceremony.

results.title: GUTA urges authorities to act over Chinese malls’ impact on local businesses
results.content: The President of the Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA), Clement Boateng, has urged authorities to examine the expansion of Chinese shopping malls, warning that local businesses are losing market share.

results.title: Obuasi abuse allegations: Coalition demands national child-protection overhaul
results.content: The National Coalition for Proper Human Sexual Rights and Family Values has called for a comprehensive overhaul of Ghana's child-protection system, warning that the allegations of sexual abuse at the Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) expose weaknesses that could leave children vulnerable in schools and other institutions.

results.title: Goods delayed, banks demanding repayment – GUTA President details traders’ pressures
results.content: Rising cargo volumes are causing port congestion and delaying goods clearance, the President of the Ghana Union of Traders’ Associations (GUTA), Clement Boateng, said.

results.title: Choose engineering over business degrees – Salem Kalmoni advises youth
results.content: Young Ghanaians have been encouraged to pursue engineering and other technical disciplines rather than follow the growing preference for business administration qualifications, which are increasingly common in the job market.

results.title: GUTA President calls for loan repayment moratorium as shipment delays hit traders
results.content: GUTA President Clement Boateng has called for a moratorium on loan repayments to give traders breathing space as shipment delays leave them facing bank demands before their goods arrive.
